body:
**Reorganization.** Group examples by geometry (`column/`, `plane/`, `sphere/`,
`hybrid/{box,plane,sphere}`); delete the Held–Suarez cases, the
potential-temperature and internal-energy variants (the total-energy form
remains), duplicated cases, and dead scripts — 28 files deleted, net −4,200
lines. Merge the CUDA shallow-water fork into `sphere/shallow_water.jl`; share
the 2D plane setup in `plane_utils.jl`, the figure-link helper in
`example_utils.jl`, and the bubble constants in `bubble_parameters.jl`; sweep
all four flux constraints in one column limiter example. Consolidate
repetitive Buildkite steps into matrices, and point figure links at
repository-root paths so they resolve in the build logs.

**Dependency removal.** Examples, tests, and the introduction tutorial
time-step with ClimaTimeSteppers 0.10; the OrdinaryDiffEq/SciML dependencies
are gone, which drops 27 packages from the Buildkite environment. The SciML
compatibility layer goes with them — breaking for anyone passing a `Field` to
an OrdinaryDiffEq integrator, recorded in NEWS.md — and the two time-stepping
tests join the curated suite under `Pkg.test`.

**Physics fixes.** Terrain-following surface flow in the mountain and channel
cases, applied between stages rather than by mutating the stage state; the
correct Exner exponent in the mountain initial density (cv/R, not cp/R — the
state was out of hydrostatic balance by a factor of π(z)); a consistent
constant-N² Exner profile in the Agnesi case; pressure rather than density in
the isothermal channel's vertical energy flux; in-place mass-matrix
normalization of the DG tendency; degrees→radians in the sphere limiter's
slot-width test.

**Assertions.** Each example now asserts what it demonstrates: exact solutions
(column cases), conservation and stability (jets, channels, mountains), bounds
(limiters), bracketed rise speeds (bubbles), unchanged fields (balanced/at-rest
cases), with measured tolerances noted in place, and runs stopped before the
configuration becomes invalid (e.g., bubble hitting lid). Limiter error norms
are normalized by the initial tracer's norm rather than pointwise, and
assertions are rank-safe under MPI: root-only diagnostics are guarded, and
peak velocities are reduced across ranks.
title: Examples: consolidate, correct, and make CI assert the physics

body:
Use CA's buildkite as a downstream test.

Remove atmos from GHA based downstream tests.

The GitHub action downstream tests for climaatmos are very flaky. They often fail due to what I believe is running out of memory. Additionally, running atmos unit tests through GHA doesn't guarantee there won't be gpu errors.  This replaces the gha based atmos downstream tests with a buildkite pipeline step that runs climaatmos buildkite ci with the relevant climacore commit.  

One downside of this is that a failure is less visible. I made the trigger a soft fail to replicate the current behavior of other downstream tests. It also makes the downstream test fail for reproducibility test failures.
title: Run atmos downgrade tests through buildkite
